To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1-acylated 5-hydroxypirazolidines form only intramolecular hydrogen bonds in the solid state, but in solution, they form intermolecular hydrogen bonding, in which the proton is accepted by the hydroxyl oxygen atom.

the acid-base properties of 5-hydroxy-1-acylpyrazolidines depend on the length of the acyl chain, the presence of the substituents in the acyl chain and the presence of the solvent, and the acid-base properties are similar to those of phenols.
the acidity and basicity of 1-phenacyl-5-phenylpyrazolidine in a hydrogen bond are similar to those of phenol.

the synthesis and properties of 1,5-diacyl-3,4-pyrazolidinediones.

the study of acid-base properties of 5-hydroxymethylpyrazolidine in the gas phase, in solutions of different polarity, in solutions in the presence of hydrogen bond acceptor (acetic acid), and in solutions in the absence of hydrogen bond acceptors (acetic acid).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the acidity in a hydroxyl group is determined by the electron density at the oxygen atom, and this density is affected by the substituents on the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl oxygen atom is bonded, as well as by the substituencies on other carbon atoms.
the 1-acylated 5-hydroxypyrroli-dines are weak bases and weak acids in a hydrogen bond, and that the acidity in a solution is determined by the acidity in a bond.
the acid-base properties of 5-acyl-3-hydroxypyridines in a hydrogen-bonded medium are similar to the corresponding properties of 1,4-dihydropyridines in a nonpolar medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1-acylpiperidines and 1-acylcyclohexanes are less acidic in a hydrogen bond than 1-acyloxazolidines and 1-acetyl-5-hydroxy-2-imidazolidones.
the proton transfer from the hydroxyl oxygen to the carbonyl oxygen in the hydrogen bond of 1-alkyl-5-acylpyrazolidines is a very fast process.
1-acylpiperidines and 1-acylsalts are more acidic in a hydrogen bond than the corresponding 1-acyloxazolidines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acidity of the hydroxypyrazolidine proton in a hydrogen bond is determined not by the substituent on the nitrogen atom but by the nature of the substituent at the acyl group.
the acidity of 1-phenyl-5-hydroxyprazolidines is comparable to that of phenols, while the acidity of 3,3-dimethyl-1-phenylpyrazolidine-5-one is comparable to that phenols.
